title: Practical Spoken English
goal: Communicate in the 21 core real-life situations — from first greetings to interviews and public speaking — with guided dialogues, role-plays and private speaking practice.

modules.title: Everyday Talk
modules.description: First conversations: greetings, introducing yourself and your family, daily routines and asking questions, at A1.

lessons.title: Greetings
objectives: Greet people at different times of day
Use hello, hi, good morning, goodbye naturally
lessons.assessment: Complete 3 greeting exchanges with correct time-of-day choice

lessons.title: Self-Introduction
objectives: Introduce yourself: name, country, job, one interest
Respond to Nice to meet you
lessons.assessment: Deliver a 5-sentence self-introduction and respond to 3 replies

lessons.title: Family Introduction
objectives: Introduce family members and their basic details
Answer 3 questions about your family
lessons.assessment: Introduce a family of 3+ members and handle 3 follow-up questions

checkpoint.criteria: Greet, introduce yourself and your family in first meetings

lessons.title: Daily Routines
objectives: Describe your day in sequence with time phrases
Ask about someone else's routine
lessons.assessment: Describe your day in 6 sentences and ask 2 routine questions

lessons.title: Asking Questions
objectives: Ask yes/no and WH-questions to get information
Show interest with follow-up questions
lessons.assessment: Conduct a 6-question mini-interview with correct forms

checkpoint.criteria: Talk about daily life and drive conversations with questions

modules.title: Getting Things Done
modules.description: Transactional speaking: asking for help, giving instructions, expressing opinions, making requests and expressing preferences.

lessons.title: Asking for Help
objectives: Ask for help politely with Can you and Could you
Offer help and respond to thanks
lessons.assessment: Make 5 help requests with appropriate politeness

lessons.title: Giving Instructions
objectives: Give step-by-step instructions with first, then, after that
Check understanding: Is that clear?
lessons.assessment: Give a 5-step process explanation with sequencing words

checkpoint.criteria: Ask for and deliver help with polite, sequenced language

lessons.title: Expressing Opinions
objectives: State opinions with I think and In my opinion
Agree and disagree politely
lessons.assessment: Express 3 opinions with reasons and respond to agreement/disagreement

lessons.title: Making Requests
objectives: Make direct and indirect requests appropriately
Handle yes and no answers gracefully
lessons.assessment: Make 5 requests across formality levels appropriately

lessons.title: Expressing Preferences
objectives: Say what you prefer with prefer, would rather and like better
Compare two options in conversation
lessons.assessment: Express and justify 4 preferences in comparison dialogues

checkpoint.criteria: Handle opinions, requests and preferences with appropriate register

modules.title: Out and About
modules.description: Situation speaking: shopping, restaurants, travel and telephone conversations at A2.

lessons.title: Shopping
objectives: Ask for products, sizes and prices
Complete a buy-something dialogue start to finish
lessons.assessment: Complete a full shop role-play: ask, choose, pay

lessons.title: Restaurants
objectives: Order a meal and drinks politely
Ask about the menu and request the bill
lessons.assessment: Complete a restaurant role-play of 8+ turns including the bill

checkpoint.criteria: Shop and order food in full transactional dialogues

lessons.title: Travel
objectives: Ask for directions and follow them
Handle tickets, platforms and basic travel problems
lessons.assessment: Complete directions and ticket role-plays with correct comprehension

lessons.title: Telephone Conversations
objectives: Answer and make calls with phone phrases
Take a simple message: name, number, reason
lessons.assessment: Complete a phone role-play and record a 3-part message accurately

checkpoint.criteria: Handle travel and telephone situations in English

modules.title: Structured Speaking
modules.description: Extended and higher-stakes speaking at B1: classroom and workplace communication, social conversation, storytelling, interviews, group discussions and public speaking.

lessons.title: Classroom Communication
objectives: Ask for clarification and repetition in class
Participate: volunteer answers, work in pairs
lessons.assessment: Use 6 clarification phrases correctly in classroom scenarios

lessons.title: Workplace Communication
objectives: Speak in meetings: state progress, raise problems, suggest
Use workplace politeness with colleagues and managers
lessons.assessment: Give a 30-second status update and raise one issue in a meeting role-play

checkpoint.criteria: Communicate in classroom and workplace settings

lessons.title: Social Conversations
objectives: Start, maintain and close small-talk conversations
Talk about free time, hobbies and weekend plans
lessons.assessment: Hold a 2-minute small-talk exchange with natural openers and closers

lessons.title: Storytelling
objectives: Tell a personal story with clear sequence and a point
Use narrative tenses and reaction-checks
lessons.assessment: Tell a 90-second personal story with clear structure

checkpoint.criteria: Hold social conversations and tell structured stories

lessons.title: Interviews
objectives: Answer the 10 most common interview questions with structure
Ask the interviewer 2 sensible questions
lessons.assessment: Complete a mock interview: 5 structured answers plus 2 questions

lessons.title: Group Discussions
objectives: Contribute to a discussion: opinions, agreements, interruptions
Invite others in and manage turns
lessons.assessment: Contribute 5 turns to a group discussion with proper phrases

lessons.title: Public Speaking
objectives: Give a short structured talk: opening, 3 points, close
Use signposting and manage nerves
lessons.assessment: Deliver a 2-minute structured mini-talk with signposting

checkpoint.criteria: Perform in interviews, discussions and short public talks

exitAssessment.title: Spoken English Exit Test
exitAssessment.criteria: A 5-minute speaking assessment covering: greetings and introductions, a transactional role-play (shop or restaurant), a telephone exchange, a 90-second personal story, 3 structured interview answers. Graded on task completion, comprehensibility and appropriateness — never on accent.
